subChunks.title: Enterprise Design System Architecture
subChunks.hookHtml: A design system that serves one team is a component library. A design system that serves ten teams, three product lines, multiple brands, and a monorepo spanning 50 engineers is an enterprise design system. The technical challenges are the same but the governance, versioning, distribution, adoption, and deprecation challenges are an order of magnitude harder.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "An enterprise design system is a product. It has customers — the teams that use it. It has a roadmap. It has versioning. It has breaking changes and migration paths. It has adoption metrics. A Lead engineer who builds a design system without this mental model will produce excellent components that nobody uses because the adoption story is nonexistent."

The three-layer architecture

packages/
  design-tokens/        # Layer 1: Primitive tokens
    src/
      tokens.json       # Figma-exported, Style Dictionary input
    dist/
      tokens.css        # CSS custom properties
      tokens.d.ts       # TypeScript types

  ui-core/             # Layer 2: Core component library
    src/
      components/      # Headless + CVA variants
      hooks/           # Shared behaviour hooks
      utils/           # cn(), formatters
    package.json

  ui-brand-acme/       # Layer 3: Brand-specific layer
    src/
      tokens.css       # Extends ui-core/tokens with Acme brand
      components/      # Acme-specific components or overrides

Semantic versioning for a design system

/* MAJOR (1.0.0 → 2.0.0): Breaking changes */
// - Removing a component or variant
// - Renaming a prop with no compatibility shim
// - Changing a token name that requires source changes

/* MINOR (1.0.0 → 1.1.0): New capabilities, backward-compatible */
// - Adding a new component
// - Adding a new variant to an existing component
// - Adding new tokens

/* PATCH (1.0.0 → 1.0.1): Bug fixes */
// - Visual fix to an existing component
// - Contrast fix, spacing adjustment
// - Token value correction

Deprecation strategy

// ❌ Hard removal without migration path
export function OldButton() { /* removed */ }

// ✅ Soft deprecation with console warning
export function OldButton(props: OldButtonProps) {
  if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
    console.warn(
      '[ui-core] OldButton is deprecated. Use Button from @my-org/ui-core/button. ' +
      'OldButton will be removed in v3.0.0.'
    );
  }
  return <Button {...mapOldProps(props)} />;
}

// ✅ Codemods for major version migrations
npx @my-org/ui-core-codemod v2-to-v3 ./src

Adoption metrics — knowing if your system works

/* Track: */
// - Component adoption rate: % of Button usages that use ui-core/Button
// - Version distribution: % of teams on current vs N-1 vs N-2
// - Usage by component: which components are used vs which exist
// - Token coverage: % of colour values that reference tokens vs arbitrary values

/* Tooling */
// - ESLint custom rules: warn on direct Tailwind colour class when token exists
// - GitHub Actions: track ui-core version in each app's package.json
// - Storybook Coverage: document which components have stories

Multi-brand token architecture

/* Layer 1: Primitives — never used directly by consumers */
@theme {
  --color-neutral-50: oklch(0.98 0 0);
  --color-neutral-950: oklch(0.10 0 0);
  --color-indigo-500: oklch(0.55 0.20 270);
}

/* Layer 2: Semantic (brand-agnostic) — what consumers use */
@theme {
  --color-surface: var(--color-neutral-50);
  --color-foreground: var(--color-neutral-950);
  --color-primary: var(--color-indigo-500);  /* overridden per-brand */
}

/* Layer 3: Brand override (Acme brand) */
@theme {
  --color-primary: oklch(0.60 0.15 160);  /* Acme's teal primary */
}
/* All components referencing --color-primary are now teal for Acme */

ESLint rules for design system enforcement

// .eslintrc design system rules
{
  "rules": {
    // Warn when a hardcoded hex colour is used instead of a token
    "no-restricted-syntax": [
      "warn",
      {
        "selector": "Literal[value=/^#[0-9a-fA-F]/]",
        "message": "Use a design token instead of a hardcoded colour value"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Solomon: "Measure adoption. Not usage — adoption. A component used 10 times out of 10 instances in the codebase is 100% adopted. A component used 10 times with 90 other instances using custom implementations is 10% adopted. You cannot manage what you do not measure."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: A design system has three failure modes: it is technically excellent but nobody adopts it; it is adopted but never maintained and rots; it is maintained but has no deprecation strategy and teams fear upgrading. An enterprise design system must solve all three simultaneously.

storyBeats.speaker: Three-layer token architecture

Build a design system governance dashboard showing the package structure, versioning, and adoption metrics:

  • .ds-grid: grid, grid-cols-1, md:grid-cols-3, gap-4, p-6
  • .ds-metric: bg-white, rounded-xl, border, border-gray-200, p-5
  • .ds-metric-label: text-xs, font-semibold, text-gray-500, uppercase, tracking-wider, mb-1
  • .ds-metric-value: text-3xl, font-bold, text-gray-900
  • .ds-metric-sub: text-xs, text-gray-500, mt-1
  • .ds-metric--good: border-l-4, border-l-emerald-500
  • .ds-metric--warn: border-l-4, border-l-amber-500
  • .ds-metric--bad: border-l-4, border-l-red-500

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design an enterprise design system health dashboard from scratch. Include: version distribution bar chart (percentage of teams on each major version), component adoption ranking (top 5 most and least adopted components), token coverage ring chart, open deprecations count, and a migration timeline. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the three-layer token architecture (primitives, semantic, brand) for a multi-brand enterprise design system. Walk through exactly what happens when the Acme brand needs its primary colour to be teal instead of indigo — which layer changes, which layers stay the same, and why components don't need to change. Then explain what 'adoption' means for a design system and why it's different from 'usage'.

questions.prompt: In semantic versioning for a design system, what triggers a MAJOR version bump?
options: Breaking changes — removing a component, renaming a prop without a compatibility shim, or changing a token name that requires consumer source changes
Any visual change to an existing component, since users may be relying on the exact appearance
Adding a new component or variant — any additive change is a major release
Releasing to production — every production release is a major version
questions.answer: Breaking changes — removing a component, renaming a prop without a compatibility shim, or changing a token name that requires consumer source changes
questions.explanation: Semantic versioning for design systems follows the same rules as software: MAJOR = breaking changes that require consumer code changes. This includes removing public API surface (components, props), renaming without backward compat shims, and token renames that require find-and-replace in consumer codebases. Teams depending on a design system need to know when an upgrade requires code changes vs when it's safe to auto-merge.

questions.prompt: The enterprise design system needs to support both 'Acme' brand (teal primary) and 'BuilderCo' brand (orange primary) from the same component codebase. What is the correct architecture?
options: Three token layers: primitives define all colours, semantic layer defines --color-primary, brand layers (one per brand) override --color-primary with the brand-specific value — all components reference --color-primary only
Two separate component libraries: one for Acme and one for BuilderCo, each with their own token definitions
A single token file with colour variables suffixed by brand: --color-primary-acme and --color-primary-builderco
Inline styles on the root element: <div style='--color-primary: teal'> wraps Acme content
questions.answer: Three token layers: primitives define all colours, semantic layer defines --color-primary, brand layers (one per brand) override --color-primary with the brand-specific value — all components reference --color-primary only
questions.explanation: The three-layer architecture is precisely designed for multi-brand scenarios. Primitives are never referenced directly in components. Semantic tokens (--color-primary) are referenced in components. Brand layers override semantic tokens per brand. Result: one component codebase serves multiple brands — change a brand token file, every component in that brand updates automatically. Maintaining two separate component libraries duplicates every bug fix and feature forever.

questions.prompt: A design system reports 95% adoption rate for its Button component. A principal engineer says this is misleading. Why?
options: Adoption rate should be measured per team, not per instance — 95% of instances may come from 2 of 10 teams while 8 teams still use custom buttons
95% adoption is excellent — the principal engineer is incorrect
Adoption rate should only count production code, not tests or Storybook stories
The metric should track render count, not source code instances
questions.answer: Adoption rate should be measured per team, not per instance — 95% of instances may come from 2 of 10 teams while 8 teams still use custom buttons
questions.explanation: Instance-based adoption counts can be skewed by high-usage teams. If 2 of 10 teams use the design system's Button 1000 times each (2000 instances) but 8 teams use custom buttons 30 times each (240 instances), the adoption rate is 2000/2240 = 89% by instance — misleadingly high. Team-based adoption (2/10 = 20%) better reflects how many teams have actually standardised. Both metrics matter; neither alone tells the full story.
